title: Error messages and logs: what must never leak

videos.script: A patient asks for a page and something breaks. The page she gets back shows a traceback. File paths, the line that failed, the name of the dictionary. {{trace}} None of that helps her. All of it helps somebody mapping the portal from outside. {{outside}} Meanwhile the server's log holds the password she typed, in plain text. {{password}} Every failure has two readers. The person who asked needs to know it failed. The team needs to know why. {{two}} Give the page a short reference. Put the detail in the log, under the same reference. And keep out of the log what nobody should read there. {{reference}} Today four tests say all of that, fail against the old code, and pass against the new. {{today}}
